Luntang 屬體鳴樂器，以敲擊五根水平圓柱原木邊緣發聲，原木依音高升序排列，: The Luntang is an idiophone: it sounds by striking the edges of five horizontal cylindrical logs, the logs arranged in ascending pitch to form a five-note scale from low to high. The principle is that the log vibrates when struck, and the sound comes from the log. The source does not state how volume is controlled, nor how its timbre differs from other instruments of the family.
Luntang是菲律賓馬京達瑙人的木琴類體鳴樂器，由五根圓柱形水平木條垂直懸掛，: The Luntang is a xylophone-type idiophone of the Magindanao of the Philippines, made of five cylindrical horizontal bars hung vertically and arranged by pitch. The player strikes the edges of the bars; it can be played solo or by two people sitting on either side. The Magindanao use it mainly for their own amusement, and at the same time to keep farmers awake and drive birds away; in the past it was also often used for long-distance communication. The Yakan call it kwintangan kayo and use it further in social interaction between the sexes.
Luntang的聆聽示範可從其使用場合理解：在馬京達瑙社群中，它主要用於自我娛樂: The Luntang's listening examples can be understood from the occasions on which it is used: among the Magindanao it is mainly for self-amusement, and it was also used in the fields to keep farmers awake and drive birds away; in the past it was used for long-distance communication as well. It can be played solo, or by two people standing on either side. The Yakan call it Kwintangan kayo and use it for social interaction between the sexes. The source mentions no particular composer or piece, so a demonstration should present the sound made by striking the edges of the cylindrical logs with a beater.

此樂器見於菲律賓馬京達瑙人與雅坎人，前者稱 luntang，後者稱 kwinta: This instrument is found among the Magindanao and the Yakan of the Philippines, the former calling it luntang and the latter kwintangan kayo. The Magindanao formerly used it for long-distance communication, and later also for their own amusement, to keep farmers awake while they guarded the fields and to drive birds away. The Yakan extended its use to social interaction between the sexes, which shows how the function of the same instrument changes between different peoples.
演奏者面向五根水平原木，依音高由低到高排列的位置操作。發聲時以敲擊原木邊緣產生聲: The player faces the five horizontal logs, which are arranged from low to high pitch. The sound is made by striking the edges of the logs; a beginner can first get to know the pitch order of each log and the striking position. It can be played solo by one person, or by two people standing on either side. The source mentions no way of holding the instrument, no details of the beater and no teaching material, so the teaching points are limited to the layout, striking the edges, and the basic operation of solo or two-person playing.
